features.name: AI production maturity
features.description: The extent to which the applicant shows real experience deploying AI or LLM systems in production with attention to reliability, evaluation, and failure modes.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
Mentions AI or LLM exposure without concrete deployment detail.
Describes shipped AI features or workflows in production.
Describes shipped AI work plus evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or trustworthiness practices.

features.name: Academic preparation
features.description: The strength or level of formal technical education the applicant presents as preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience only, with no advanced degree presented.
Master's degree in computer science or a related field is presented.
Doctoral degree in computer science or a related field is presented.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Direct experience designing or owning agent-based systems, including their control boundaries, supervision, and surrounding infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic or autonomous-tooling experience is mentioned.
Agents or automation are mentioned vaguely, with little architectural detail.
The letter shows clear experience building agent-based workflows or pipelines.
The letter gives a detailed agentic architecture, such as bounded actions, contracts, logging, auditing, permissions, or a clear Go and Python division of responsibility.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Practical command of data structures and algorithms as demonstrated through concrete engineering improvements or problem solving.

levels.descriptor: No evidence of algorithmic strength is given.
The letter claims strength in algorithms or data structures without a concrete example.
The letter gives one clear example of algorithmic or data-structure improvement.
The letter gives multiple or especially strong examples tied to meaningful system simplification, performance, or correctness gains.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Whether the applicant frames security engineering as helping developers succeed through secure defaults, usable tooling, and reduced friction rather than policing.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Engineering rigor
features.description: The extent to which the letter emphasizes maintainability, operability, testing, reliability, and disciplined long-term system care.

levels.descriptor: Shows no explicit maintainability or reliability orientation.
Implies care for quality but not as a recurring theme.
Clearly values maintainable, dependable systems or draws on maintenance experience.
Makes long-term operability a central lens, emphasizing inheritance, quiet resilience, or higher standards for security-critical software.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: How concrete, technically grounded, and example-backed the letter's claims are rather than generic or unsupported.

levels.descriptor: Mostly relies on self-assertion, with little concrete support for claims.
Includes some specifics, but few mechanics, numbers, or outcomes.
Provides several concrete examples with technical detail, counts, or before-and-after effects.
Repeatedly grounds claims in vivid, trust-building evidence, including technical mechanics and clear impact.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: How central and substantial Go appears in the applicant's real production work.

levels.descriptor: Go is only briefly mentioned or not tied to meaningful ownership.
Go appears in recent work but not as a dominant language.
Go is clearly a main language for backend or service work.
Go is framed as the primary or daily-driver language with substantial system ownership.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: How clearly the letter states the concrete outcomes, effects, or consequences of the applicant's work rather than only listing activities.

levels.descriptor: Lists tasks with no visible outcomes.
Hints at benefit but remains mostly activity-based.
States clear outcomes such as reduced manual work, faster systems, or fewer bugs.
Shows strong leverage language, tying work to capacity, attention saved, or meaningful organizational effect.

features.name: Narrative cohesion
features.description: Whether the letter presents a memorable, well-structured story or thesis rather than a disconnected checklist of qualifications.

levels.descriptor: Reads as flat, list-like, or heavily templated prose.
Is competent and readable, but largely generic in voice.
Has a noticeable hook, framing device, or coherent personal story.
Has a strong, memorable voice that reinforces fit without sacrificing substance.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Ongoing attacker-oriented skill building, such as CTFs or similar hands-on offensive security practice, outside ordinary software work.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional or casual CTF participation or similar practice.
The letter shows regular CTF participation or sustained offensive practice.
The letter shows strong competitive results or especially serious, ongoing offensive-security practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Responsibility for contributing to, maintaining, or stewarding software used beyond the applicant's employer.

levels.descriptor: No open-source activity is mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches or minor contributions.
Shows regular contributions or maintainership of a small project.
Maintains a project with outside users or community responsibilities such as reviews, releases, issue handling, or roadmap decisions.

features.name: Ownership level
features.description: The degree of autonomy, seniority, and direct ownership the applicant claims over the systems or work described.

levels.descriptor: Mostly aspirational language or support-role contribution.
Shows some hands-on contribution but limited ownership.
Shows clear ownership of tools, systems, or reviews.
Shows repeated architecture, design, or lead responsibility with independent judgment.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: The technical ambition, scope, and seriousness of self-directed projects described outside the applicant's day job.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Motivation for foundational platform or infrastructure work whose impact compounds across many teams, products, or users.

levels.descriptor: Does not show any particular interest in foundational or shared systems work.
Mentions scale or impact in passing, but not as a central motivation.
Explicitly values platform or infrastructure work because it benefits many teams.
Persuasively frames central tooling as a multiplier, emphasizing inherited impact or organization-wide capacity gains.

features.name: Production delivery scope
features.description: The depth and breadth of hands-on responsibility the applicant shows for shipping, maintaining, operating, and launching production systems.

levels.descriptor: The letter shows only minimum-qualifying experience or limited production launch ownership, typically around 2 to 3 years and few services.
The letter shows solid early-career production work with some testing, maintenance, and launch ownership.
The letter shows substantial production scope, typically around 5 years or repeated ownership across several services.
The letter shows extensive production scope with long tenure and broad multi-service responsibility, often 7 or more years or many launches.

features.name: Professional tenure
features.description: The amount of relevant post-school professional software-engineering experience the applicant claims.

levels.descriptor: Below the role minimum or unclear on relevant experience length.
Roughly meets the minimum, around 2 to 3 years of relevant experience.
Shows solid mid-level experience, around 4 to 5 years.
Shows strong experience depth, around 6 or more years.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: How concretely and deeply the letter shows Python as a serious implementation language for production systems, tooling, or automation.

levels.descriptor: No Python experience is mentioned.
Mentions Python briefly or only as light scripting.
Describes regular Python use for tooling, automation, or services.
Shows deep Python ownership across production services or critical internal tooling.

features.name: Requirement mapping
features.description: How explicitly the letter connects the applicant's background to the posting's stated requirements and responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: Leaves the reader to infer most of the match to the posting.
Mentions relevant experience but ties it only loosely to the role.
Directly connects several experiences or skills to stated requirements or responsibilities.
Explicitly walks through the posting match in a structured, requirement-aware way.

features.name: Role-specific motivation
features.description: How specifically and convincingly the letter explains why this exact role and team are a compelling fit for the applicant.

levels.descriptor: The motivation is formulaic and could fit almost any software-engineering application.
The letter shows some interest in security or Google, but the rationale is still fairly generic.
The letter gives clear, role-relevant motivation tied to the team's mission, working model, or problem space.
The letter gives memorable, well-tailored motivation that shows the applicant has thought specifically about this team's security-automation challenge.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: The depth of direct hands-on experience assessing systems for security issues and validating or following through on remediation.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention security assessment work.
Refers to reviews or security thinking vaguely without concrete methods.
Describes performing assessments such as threat modeling, code review, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows structured assessment practice with clear methods and follow-through such as remediation validation or recurring ownership.

features.name: Security automation framing
features.description: How clearly the letter understands the role as scaling scarce security expertise through automation and frames the team's problem in those terms.

levels.descriptor: Does not clearly articulate security automation as a central problem of the role.
Mentions reducing manual toil or automating repetitive work in general terms.
Clearly frames the role as scaling response capacity, expert attention, or organization-wide security effort.
Shows nuanced systems thinking about automation, such as variant analysis, triage strategy, scarce-expert amplification, or vulnerability response as a design problem.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: The presence and rigor of formal external security certifications or credentialing the applicant cites.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A baseline credential such as Security+ is presented.
A hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP is presented.

features.name: Security engineering philosophy
features.description: The maturity of the applicant's broader security worldview, including principled reasoning about secure systems and authentic identification with security work.

levels.descriptor: Offers no distinct philosophy about the quality bar required for security engineering.
Makes only generic statements about reliability or security importance.
Expresses a clear philosophy of quiet resilience, dependable systems, or a higher standard for security tooling.
Builds a memorable, well-integrated case that security tooling demands exceptional rigor and ties that belief to prior work or design choices.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Hands-on experience building software that automates vulnerability intake, classification, routing, deduplication, or related security-response workflows.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not describe vulnerability-handling automation.
The letter mentions security automation in general, but not a specific vulnerability triage workflow.
The letter shows direct experience automating intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.
The letter shows a clear transformation of a manual vulnerability workflow or explicitly states operational impact from the automation.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: The degree to which the letter is free of distracting spelling, grammar, typo, and copy-editing errors.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors repeatedly interrupt reading or seriously undermine credibility.
Noticeable proofreading problems distract the reader more than once.
Contains some typos, but the letter remains easy to follow.
Mostly clean, with at most a minor slip.
Polished and effectively error-free at a professional standard.

other.name: Other
other.description: Genuinely idiosyncratic dimensions that do not clearly share an underlying construct with any larger recurring group.

levels.descriptor: No additional languages are mentioned.
Mentions 1 to 2 additional languages.
Mentions 3 to 5 additional languages.
Mentions more than 5 additional languages.
